passage.title: Reading Part 2 - Test 07
passage.text:
Color is far more than a visual experience; it has the power to influence our emotions, behaviors, and even our physical reactions. The field of color psychology studies how different colors affect human mood and decision-making. From the clothes we wear to the design of our homes and workplaces, color choices can have profound effects on our daily lives.

Research has shown that warm colors like red, orange, and yellow tend to evoke feelings of energy, excitement, and warmth. Red, in particular, is associated with passion and urgency, which is why it's often used in warning signs and sale advertisements. However, these colors can also increase heart rate and blood pressure, making them potentially overwhelming in large doses. In contrast, cool colors such as blue, green, and purple generally promote feelings of calmness and relaxation. Blue is frequently used in bedrooms and offices because it can enhance focus and productivity while reducing stress.

The effects of color are not universal, however; cultural background plays a significant role in how people interpret colors. In Western cultures, white is associated with purity and is commonly worn at weddings, while in some Eastern cultures, white is the color of mourning. Similarly, red symbolizes good luck and prosperity in China but may represent danger or warning in Western contexts. These cultural differences highlight the importance of considering the audience when using color in design and communication.

Businesses have long understood the power of color psychology in marketing and branding. Fast-food restaurants often use red and yellow in their logos and interiors because these colors stimulate appetite and create a sense of urgency that encourages quick dining. Luxury brands tend to favor black, gold, and silver to convey sophistication and exclusivity. Even small changes in color can significantly impact consumer behavior—studies have found that simply changing the color of a "Buy Now" button on a website can increase or decrease purchase rates. As our understanding of color psychology continues to grow, its applications in design, marketing, and everyday life become increasingly sophisticated.
